## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

While secondary search results for this title yielded only incidental mentions of Ānanda in narrative contexts or accidental homographs of the Sanskrit ablative *ānandāt* in Tantric treatises, the text's internal and cross-tradition textual connections are thoroughly documented in canonical and comparative records [DharmaNexus].

 Sutta parallels include *Itivuttaka* 86 (*Dhammānudhammapaṭipanna Sutta*), *Dīgha Nikāya* 16 (*Mahāparinibbāna Sutta*), and *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 6.15 (*Parinibbānasutta*), as well as a Sanskrit narrative parallel in the *Mahāvastu* (The Jātaka of Asthisena) and a thematic resemblance to the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547).

 Within the *Theragāthā* itself, DharmaNexus identifies reuse between §2.4–4.1 and verses in the *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1) and the *Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.4) [DharmaNexus].
